Bandwidth Usage Modeling and Reporting

Statistical Modeling and Systems Engineering · 2026 · Historical analysis and live reporting · 3 min read

Packaged a system that scores homelab traffic against a residential usage model and produces dated JSON and one-page reports.

Overview

Published OpenVault usage summaries provide the statistical reference; pfSense/vnStat provides live measurements. A frozen scorer estimates monthly exceedance and model-relative incidence for total, download, and upload traffic.

Problem

Multi-terabyte repository mirrors and planned cloud-backup uploads raised a practical question: how unusual was this usage? Aggregated, right-skewed source data could not support a raw Gaussian z-score or universal ISP limit.

Constraints

  • Fit aggregate reports without household-level observations or a known outlier population
  • Expose uncertainty in extreme and directional estimates
  • Score vnStat exports without implying an ISP enforcement threshold
  • Keep model regeneration separate from routine reporting

Approach

Extracted summaries from nine reports spanning 1Q24–1Q26, tested lognormal and Weibull fits, then selected a segmented gamma model with a Pareto tail. Frozen parameters score vnStat counters; restricted SFTP and systemd automation deliver scored JSON and printable PostScript.

Key Decisions

Report exceedance probability and model-relative incidence instead of raw sigma

Reasoning:

The source lacks a suitable observed standard deviation. A survival curve answers how common a measured volume is under the fitted model.

Alternatives considered:
  • Use mean and standard deviation as a Gaussian score
  • Set green, yellow, and red bands from anecdotal ISP thresholds

Use a segmented gamma model with a Pareto tail

Reasoning:

The lognormal missed low-usage buckets; Weibull improved the fit, while the selected gamma/gamma structure matched buckets more closely. The 5,000 GB tail remains extrapolative.

Alternatives considered:
  • Single lognormal fit
  • Single Weibull fit

Freeze evaluated parameters and separate the reporter from receiver automation

Reasoning:

RPM builds reuse evaluated weights, while separate service identities limit the upload account's access.

Alternatives considered:
  • Refit the model during every report run
  • Run upload reception and reporting under one account

Tech Stack

  • Python
  • SciPy
  • Jupyter
  • pfSense/vnStat
  • systemd
  • RPM
  • PostScript

Result & Impact

  • 504
    Model configurations
  • 1,008
    Period-level fits
  • ~153 s
    Recorded grid runtime

Dated JSON and one-page reports compare measured homelab traffic with a consistent reference curve.

Learnings

  • Matching the mean by construction is not validation; bucket shares exposed the lognormal failure
  • Low bucket error does not make far-tail or directional projections precise
  • Freezing parameters keeps model changes deliberate and reviewable

What the Numbers Mean

The scorer estimates the fraction of households in its modeled reference distribution that would use at least a measured monthly volume. “1 in N” is its reciprocal, not an observed subscriber count or ISP warning. Directional tails have less validation. The 1Q27 reference is a projection, and rare estimates depend heavily on the Pareto tail.
